summary: Repaired and enabled the restricted Unix-socket status service on node1. Authorized users receive the preserved status document, invalid requests receive ERROR, and outsider access is denied. Restart persistence was verified.
actions_performed: Provisioned statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers.
Repaired server.py to accept only STATUS followed by a newline.
Configured statusd.service to run as statusd:status-readers and start automatically.
Set status.sock permissions to 0660 with owner statusd and group status-readers.
Preserved status.txt content; its SHA-256 remained 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b.
Restarted node1 safely and verified service recovery without changing RHEL 10.0 or kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

evidence.requirement: Authorized owner and group-member access; outsider exclusion; protocol behavior
evidence.summary: statusd and status-reader roles are correct; socket is 0660 statusd:status-readers; STATUS\n returns the document, invalid input returns ERROR\n, and outsider receives PermissionError.
The document SHA-256 was identical before repair, after repair, and after restart.

Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 to 0556ef04-37d6-4bbf-8655-83ca549201fc; enabled service, socket, document response, protocol validation, and access boundary all recovered.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
